title: Welcome to C!
description: Write a simple C program that prints a warm greeting message to the standard output. The message should be 'Welcome to C Programming!' followed by a newline character.
constraints: None. The program should simply print the specified string.
explanation: The greeting is printed using printf.

title: Display Your Age and Height
description: Declare an integer variable `age` and a floating-point variable `height`. Assign your current age (e.g., 30) to `age` and your height in meters (e.g., 1.75) to `height`. Then, print both values in a formatted string.
constraints: Age will be a positive integer. Height will be a positive floating-point number.
sample_output: My age is 30 years and my height is 1.75 meters.
explanation: The age and height are printed in a formatted message.

title: Sum, Difference, and Product of Two Numbers
description: Develop a C program that prompts the user to enter two whole numbers. Read these two integers from the standard input. Subsequently, calculate their sum, their difference (first minus second), and their product, then print each result on its own line.
constraints: Input integers will be between -1000 and 1000. Ensure robust input handling if necessary, though basic `scanf` is sufficient for this level.
explanation: The sum, difference, and product of the two numbers are calculated and printed.

title: Read and Display a Single Character and Its ASCII Value
description: Create a C program that asks the user to input a single character. Read this character from the keyboard using `scanf()`. After reading, print the character back to the console and also print its ASCII value.
constraints: Input will be a single printable ASCII character. The character should be read without issues related to leftover newline characters from previous inputs.
sample_output: You entered character: A, Its ASCII Value: 65
explanation: The input character and its ASCII value are printed.

title: Circumference and Area of a Circle
description: Write a C program that calculates the circumference and area of a circle. Prompt the user to enter the radius (a floating-point number) of the circle. Use the mathematical formulas for circumference and area.
constraints: Input radius will be a positive floating-point number (e.g., 0.1 to 100.0).
explanation: The circumference and area are calculated and printed to two decimals.

title: Temperature Conversion: Celsius to Fahrenheit and Kelvin
description: Develop a C program that converts a temperature given in Celsius to both Fahrenheit and Kelvin. Prompt the user to enter the temperature in Celsius (a floating-point number). Apply the necessary formulas and print both converted values.
constraints: Input temperature will be between -100.0 and 500.0 Celsius.
sample_output:
Temperature in Celsius: 25.00 C
Temperature in Fahrenheit: 77.00 F
Temperature in Kelvin: 298.15 K
explanation: The temperature is converted to Fahrenheit and Kelvin and printed.

title: Swapping Two Numbers Without a Temporary Variable
description: Write a C program that takes two integer numbers, `num1` and `num2`, as input from the user. Your task is to swap their values without using any third or temporary variable. Print the values before and after swapping.
constraints: Input integers will be between -500 and 500. Ensure the method chosen works correctly for all integer ranges within typical `int` limits, including zero or negative numbers if needed.
sample_output:
Before swapping: num1 = 5, num2 = 10
After swapping: num1 = 10, num2 = 5
explanation: The variables are swapped using arithmetic operations without a temp variable.

title: Input Buffer Flushing: Reading Integer then Character
description: Write a C program that first prompts the user to enter an integer, and immediately after, prompts them to enter a single character. Print both the integer and the character that were entered. Handle the input buffer correctly.
constraints: The integer will be between 1 and 100. The character will be any printable ASCII character. The solution should explicitly address the newline character issue.
sample_output:
You entered integer: 123
You entered character: A
explanation: After reading the integer, the input buffer is cleared before reading the character.

title: Simple Product Price Calculator with Sales Tax
description: Imagine you're building a basic point-of-sale system. Write a C program that calculates the total cost of an item including sales tax. Prompt the user to enter the `item_price` and `quantity`, then compute and print the subtotal, tax amount, and total cost.
constraints: Item Price: 0.01 to 1000.00. Quantity: 1 to 100. Sales tax rate is a constant 0.05.
explanation: Subtotal, tax, and total are calculated and printed with two decimals.
